samples.summary: New read-side nesting cap has no matching write-side cap: a truncated table written back prunes the peer's deeper rows from the CRDT
samples.evidence: `treeNodeToBlock` now reads a table nested past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` as `rows: []` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:483, crdt-tree.ts:228), but the in-memory `Block` produced that way is the same object the write path serializes back: `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1680) does `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block))`, replacing the whole block subtree with what `buildBlockNode` (line 364/375) derives from `block.tableData.rows`. Any `doc.updateBlockDirect(...)` on an ancestor table (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4185, 4743) therefore rewrites the truncated shape into the tree and permanently deletes everything below level 32 for every peer. The backend writer has the same shape (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:150-200). Truncation-on-read is recoverable; truncation written back is not.

samples.summary: DOCX import recurses into nested tables with no depth cap, so the producer the layout comment names can still overflow the stack and can create documents deeper than the reader will ever show
samples.evidence: `table-layout.ts`'s new comment says the layout bounds itself because "the layout takes documents from other producers too (DOCX import, paste)". That producer is `DocxImporter.convertTable`, which recurses unbounded at packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:415 (`cellBlocks.push(DocxImporter.convertTable(childEl, imageUrls))`) — a crafted .docx overflows the stack during import, before any layout runs, so the layout cap never sees it. A merely deep (say 40-level) import also succeeds, is written into the CRDT by the uncapped `buildBlockNode` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:375), and is then silently truncated to 32 on the next read. No cap exists on any producer side.

samples.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts) now folds with `reduce` because "`Math.max(...rows)` throws `RangeError` past ~100k arguments, and the row count is a peer's to choose". The same computation on the model path was not changed: packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:57 does `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1`. samples.summary: Shift+click now resolves the gesture against the body layout while the anchor's cell info comes from the active (possibly header/footer) layout
samples.evidence: The shift+click branch takes `anchorCellInfo` from `this.getCellInfo(anchor.blockId)`, which reads `getActiveLayout()` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3793), then hands it to `resolveCellGesture`, which resolves everything against `this.getLayout()` (the body layout, packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3945-3953 region). With the edit context on header/footer and a click landing on a body table, the two maps describe different documents, so the comparison of `resolvedCellInfo.tableBlockId` to `anchorTableId` is made across layouts. The prior inline code compared row/col only. The gesture still degrades to a caret move rather than corrupting state, so impact is low; worth confirming which layout `resolveCellGesture` should read.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate at every cited location. The new read cap truncates a nested table to `rows: []` at depth >= 32 (yorkie-doc-store.ts:479-484; crdt-tree.ts:224-229), but the write path has no corresponding cap: `buildBlockNode` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:364-376) recurses unbounded over `block.tableData.rows`, and `updateBlock` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1666-1686) replaces the whole block subtree via `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block))`. Reachable read-modify-write round trips exist outside the diff: text-editor.ts:4171→4185 (clear selected cell range) and 4721→4743 (paste cells into table) both `doc.getBlock(tableBlockId)` from the capped reader, mutate, and `updateBlockDirect` (document.ts:765-768) straight back into `store.updateBlock`. Nothing prevents a >32-level chain from existing: `insertTableInCell` (document.ts:885-895) applies no depth limit, `bandBlockNumerics`' MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH (numeric-attrs.ts:408) is only wired into slides/board stores, and the layout cap (table-layout.ts:145) only stops painting. So an edit to an ancestor table permanently prunes everything below level 32 for all peers — a round-trip invariant broken at sites the diff never shows. In-lane (behaviour change to a reader whose serializer consumer was not updated) and major under the rubric: silent, unrecoverable data loss at the other call site.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `DocxImporter.convertTable` (packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:246) takes no depth argument and recurses into nested `w:tbl` elements at :415 with no bound, so a crafted/deep .docx recurses unbounded during import — before any layout or CRDT reader cap applies. The import result is carried unmodified through importDocx (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docx-actions.ts:22-39) and pending-imports.ts, then written by buildBlockNode/buildCellNode/buildRowNode (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:364-414, invoked at :3221), none of which takes a depth or references MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH — even though the same file imports that constant at :57 and applies it only on the read side (:480). Thus a >32-deep imported document persists into the CRDT and is silently truncated by the readers (crdt-tree.ts:225, table-layout.ts:145). I enumerated every MAX_* constant in packages/docs/src and every MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH reference repo-wide; the only producer-side nesting cap is on the paste path (clipboard.ts:71 MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8, enforced at :308), which is not on the DOCX import path and therefore does not refute the claim — it only makes the finding's incidental closing phrase ("no cap on any producer side") inaccurate for paste. In lane for blast radius: the new layout guard's own comment names DOCX import as a producer it cannot trust, and that producer reaches the persisted structure without passing any equivalent bound; impact is a crash during import plus silent content loss on the next read.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim: packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:56-59 computes maxCol as `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1`, spreading one argument per table row. Its view-path twin at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:134-138 was deliberately converted to a `reduce` fold with an in-tree comment stating `Math.max(...rows)` throws RangeError past ~100k arguments because the row count is peer-chosen — so the hazard is acknowledged in the repo, and only one of the two paths was hardened. The model path is reachable from both the read (packages/docs/src/model/range-runs.ts:81) and the write (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:700), operating on `tableBlock.tableData.rows`, i.e. peer-written CRDT content. I could find no guard bounding row count: numeric-attrs.ts caps columns (MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS = 256 at packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:95, enforced via .slice at :256 and :380) and spans (MAX_TABLE_SPAN at :92), but the band walk iterates `table.rows` untruncated (numeric-attrs.ts:383-384), and a repo-wide search for row caps turned up only unrelated backend query limits. Doc.insertRow (document.ts:958) only guards against 0-row tables. A sibling consumer left on the unsafe form of a contract the diff hardened elsewhere is in the blast-radius lane, and the impact — RangeError thrown out of every style apply / style-summary read for such a document — is a genuine broken-site outcome. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Cycle guard added to every view-side blockParentMap walk, but `Doc.findBlockInCells` still recurses over the same map unbounded — a cyclic chain overflows the stack instead of returning undefined
finding.evidence: This delta extends the `resolveNestedTableLayout` cycle guard to two more walks (`peer-cursor.ts:129`, `selection.ts:133`), on the stated premise that a looping parent chain is representable because block ids come verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes. The model-side walk over the *same* data never got that guard: `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:276` does `tableBlock = this.findBlockInCells(cellInfo.tableBlockId);` with no visited set, so for a map containing a->b and b->a the call recurses forever and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the recursive-walk fallback at :287 can run. The map it reads is exactly the layout-derived, peer-id-keyed map: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1703` pushes the merged body+header+footer `blockParentMap` into `doc.setBlockParentMap`, and the merge across regions makes an A->B / B->A pair even easier to form than within one region. `findBlockInCells` is on the hot path for every `doc.getBlock`/`findBlock` of a cell block (typing, deletion, paste), so the crash is reachable wherever the delta's own threat model says the cycle is. Fix belongs on document.ts, mirroring the `seen` set the other three walks now carry (see `range-slices.ts:80` which already does).

verdict.reason: The finding claims `Doc.findBlockInCells` recurses over `_blockParentMap` with no visited set, so a cyclic parent chain overflows the stack. The code is not as described. `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:271-274` declares `findBlockInCells(blockId: string, seen: Set<string> = new Set([blockId]))` — a visited set seeded with the starting id — and `document.ts:288-290` guards the recursive step with `if (!tableBlock && !seen.has(cellInfo.tableBlockId)) { seen.add(cellInfo.tableBlockId); tableBlockx= this.findBlockInCells(cellInfo.tableBlockId, seen); }`. For the finding's own a->b/b->a map the walk terminates at the second hop and falls through to the bounded fallback at document.ts:301-303 (`walkCellsForBlock` over body/header/footer), returning a block or `undefined` — precisely the behaviour the reviewer says is unreachable, so no RangeError occurs. The specific evidence quoted does not exist in source: document.ts:276 is a comment line, not `tableBlock = this.findBlockInCells(cellInfo.tableBlockId);`. That unguarded form appears only in an archived design note, docs/tasks/archive/2026/04/20260413-nested-tables-todo.md:186, which quotes an older revision of the function. A repo-wide grep for `findBlockInCells` shows exactly one implementation, so there is no second unguarded copy; the adjacent map readers `siblingBlocksOf` (document.ts:332-338) and `getParentTableBlock` (document.ts:355-358) do a single map lookup then call `findBlock`, which routes into the guarded function and does not self-recurse.
